scopeAuthority.rule: Core questions must map to an Advanced knowledge topic/objective. CARs Part IX/other CARs provide legal authority; TC AIM/NAV CANADA/ISED/Standards 921/922 provide supporting operational material where applicable.

questions.question: In Canadian Class D airspace, ATC normally provides separation between:
choices: IFR aircraft; VFR traffic receives traffic information and conflict-resolution assistance as workload permits
questions.rationale: Class D permits IFR and VFR. IFR traffic receives ATC separation; VFR receives information and assistance rather than full VFR-to-VFR separation.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Class D permits IFR and VFR. IFR traffic receives ATC separation; VFR receives information and assistance rather than full VFR-to-VFR separation.

questions.question: Which flight rules are permitted in Class C airspace?
choices: Both IFR and VFR, subject to the applicable ATC requirements
questions.rationale: Class C is controlled airspace used by both IFR and VFR traffic, with communications/clearance requirements.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Class C is controlled airspace used by both IFR and VFR traffic, with communications/clearance requirements.

questions.question: Before an Advanced RPAS operation enters controlled airspace, the RPAS pilot must obtain:
choices: Authorization from the air traffic services provider responsible for the airspace
questions.rationale: CAR 901.71 requires authorization from the applicable ATS provider before an Advanced RPAS operation in controlled airspace.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.71 requires authorization from the applicable ATS provider before an Advanced RPAS operation in controlled airspace.

questions.question: If ATS requires two-way aeronautical radio communications for an RPAS operation, the person operating the radio should hold:
choices: The appropriate aeronautical radio operator qualification, such as ROC-A
questions.rationale: TP 15263 and ISED ROC-A material identify the aeronautical operator certificate as the applicable qualification for aeronautical-band voice radio operation.
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 and ISED ROC-A material identify the aeronautical operator certificate as the applicable qualification for aeronautical-band voice radio operation.

questions.question: A VFR aircraft entering Class C airspace normally requires:
questions.rationale: Class C VFR entry is subject to ATC clearance and communications requirements.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Class C VFR entry is subject to ATC clearance and communications requirements.

questions.question: Where should a pilot verify the dimensions and classification of Canadian controlled airspace?
choices: Current aeronautical charts and publications such as the VNC/VTA, DAH and CFS
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires pilots to use current aeronautical charts and approved publications to identify airspace and aerodromes.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires pilots to use current aeronautical charts and approved publications to identify airspace and aerodromes.

questions.question: Before using an aerodrome for a crewed-aircraft takeoff or landing, the PIC must ensure:
choices: The aerodrome has a control tower
The aerodrome is suitable for the intended operation
The aerodrome is in Class C
questions.rationale: CAR and TC AIM aerodrome procedures place responsibility on the PIC to determine suitability for the intended operation.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: TC AIM RAC / AGA - Aerodrome Operations
questions.learningObjective: CAR and TC AIM aerodrome procedures place responsibility on the PIC to determine suitability for the intended operation.
questions.source: TC AIM RAC / AGA - Aerodrome Operations

questions.question: In Class C airspace, ATC separation is provided between:
choices: IFR aircraft and, as prescribed, between IFR and VFR aircraft
questions.rationale: Class C provides a higher level of ATC service than Class D, including IFR/VFR separation as specified in the airspace rules.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Class C provides a higher level of ATC service than Class D, including IFR/VFR separation as specified in the airspace rules.

questions.question: For an RPAS model subject to a safety-assurance declaration, information about hazards capable of causing serious injury belongs primarily in:
choices: Safety/operating documentation supporting the declared operation
questions.rationale: Standard 922 requires technical safety assurance and supporting documentation appropriate to the declared operation.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Standard 922 requires technical safety assurance and supporting documentation appropriate to the declared operation.

questions.question: A manufacturer/declarant must retain verification evidence primarily to demonstrate:
choices: Compliance of the RPAS model with the applicable technical requirements
questions.rationale: The declaration system depends on documented verification that the model meets the applicable Standard 922 requirements.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: The declaration system depends on documented verification that the model meets the applicable Standard 922 requirements.

questions.question: A Class E control zone begins:
questions.rationale: A control zone, regardless of whether it is Class C, D or E, is controlled airspace extending upward from the surface; exact dimensions are published.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: A control zone, regardless of whether it is Class C, D or E, is controlled airspace extending upward from the surface; exact dimensions are published.

questions.question: An RPAS operating manual should identify the effects of foreseeable environmental conditions because:
choices: It is needed only for insurance
Weather can affect aircraft, C2 link, sensors, batteries and pilot performance
questions.rationale: TP 15263 and Standard 922 require pilots/operators to understand environmental limitations and performance effects.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 and Standard 922 require pilots/operators to understand environmental limitations and performance effects.

questions.question: In Southern Domestic Airspace, Class B airspace is generally found:
choices: From 12,500 ft ASL up to the floor of Class A where designated
questions.rationale: TC AIM RAC describes Class B as controlled low-level airspace, generally from 12,500 ft ASL up to Class A where designated.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TC AIM RAC describes Class B as controlled low-level airspace, generally from 12,500 ft ASL up to Class A where designated.

questions.question: Safety-related mandatory actions issued for an RPAS model are intended to:
choices: Address identified conditions affecting continued safe operation
questions.rationale: The declaration/continued-safety framework requires safety-relevant actions and information to be maintained and communicated.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: The declaration/continued-safety framework requires safety-relevant actions and information to be maintained and communicated.

questions.question: A control zone described as Class D normally extends:
choices: From the surface to its published upper limit
From 400 ft AGL to 1,000 ft AGL
questions.rationale: Control zones extend upward from the surface; their exact ceiling and lateral dimensions are published in aeronautical information.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Control zones extend upward from the surface; their exact ceiling and lateral dimensions are published in aeronautical information.

questions.question: For a VFR crewed aircraft entering Class D airspace, the normal communication requirement is:
choices: Call the airport manager by phone after landing
Establish two-way radio communication with the appropriate ATC unit before entry
questions.rationale: Class D VFR entry normally requires establishing two-way communication; unlike Class C, a specific VFR clearance is not generally the entry trigger.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Class D VFR entry normally requires establishing two-way communication; unlike Class C, a specific VFR clearance is not generally the entry trigger.

questions.question: The normal altitude ceiling for an RPAS under CAR 901.25, absent an applicable exception or authorization, is:
questions.rationale: CAR 901.25 establishes the normal 400 ft AGL limit, with defined exceptions/authorization pathways.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.25 establishes the normal 400 ft AGL limit, with defined exceptions/authorization pathways.

questions.question: At a controlled aerodrome, crewed aircraft must comply with:
choices: ATC clearances and instructions applicable to taxi, takeoff and landing
questions.rationale: Controlled aerodrome operations are subject to ATC clearances/instructions under CARs and TC AIM procedures.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Controlled aerodrome operations are subject to ATC clearances/instructions under CARs and TC AIM procedures.

questions.question: Class C airspace boundaries are shown primarily on:
choices: Current VNC/VTA and other applicable aeronautical charts/publications
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to identify controlled airspace from aeronautical charts.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to identify controlled airspace from aeronautical charts.

questions.question: Class A airspace in Canadian high-level airspace is reserved for:
questions.rationale: Class A is controlled high-level airspace in which only IFR operations are permitted.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Class A is controlled high-level airspace in which only IFR operations are permitted.

questions.question: Terminal control areas classified as Class C:
choices: Have dimensions individually published; there is no single universal altitude band for every TCA
Always extend surface to 3,000 ft AAE
questions.rationale: Canadian controlled-airspace dimensions are designated and published; pilots must use current charts/DAH rather than assume a universal vertical range.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Canadian controlled-airspace dimensions are designated and published; pilots must use current charts/DAH rather than assume a universal vertical range.

questions.question: An operation can require an SFOC-RPAS when:
choices: It falls within a category listed in CAR 903.01 or the Minister determines an SFOC is necessary for aviation safety
The operation occurs on private property
questions.rationale: CAR 903.01 defines SFOC-required categories and includes Ministerial determination where necessary for aviation safety.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 903.01 defines SFOC-required categories and includes Ministerial determination where necessary for aviation safety.

questions.question: RPAS operation at an advertised event is governed through:
choices: The applicable SFOC/event provisions of Part IX
questions.rationale: Advertised-event operations are among the special operations addressed by the SFOC framework.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Advertised-event operations are among the special operations addressed by the SFOC framework.

questions.question: The purpose of emergency/contingency procedures in an SFOC application is to:
choices: Define how abnormal and emergency situations will be managed safely
questions.rationale: CAR 903.02 requires operational and risk information sufficient to assess safe conduct, including emergency procedures where applicable.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 903.02 requires operational and risk information sufficient to assess safe conduct, including emergency procedures where applicable.

questions.question: The period for retaining safety-assurance records is determined by:
questions.rationale: Record retention is part of the regulatory declaration/verification framework and should be taken from the current CAR/Standard text.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Record retention is part of the regulatory declaration/verification framework and should be taken from the current CAR/Standard text.

questions.question: Some Class C or D control zones can change classification when the ATC unit closes. The pilot should determine the current status from:
choices: Published aeronautical information and any applicable NOTAMs
questions.rationale: Airspace classification may be conditional on unit operating hours; pilots must use current published information and NOTAMs.
questions.learningObjective: Airspace classification may be conditional on unit operating hours; pilots must use current published information and NOTAMs.

questions.question: Canadian Domestic Airspace is divided into:
choices: Northern Domestic Airspace and Southern Domestic Airspace
questions.rationale: TC AIM describes the NDA and SDA division, with different heading/reference conventions in northern regions.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: TC AIM RAC - Canadian Domestic Airspace
questions.learningObjective: TC AIM describes the NDA and SDA division, with different heading/reference conventions in northern regions.
questions.source: TC AIM RAC - Canadian Domestic Airspace

questions.question: ESCAT stands for:
choices: Emergency Scheduled Control of Air Transport
Electronic Surveillance Control of Air Traffic
Emergency Security Control of Air Traffic
questions.rationale: ESCAT is the Emergency Security Control of Air Traffic plan.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: ESCAT is the Emergency Security Control of Air Traffic plan.

questions.question: If ESCAT restrictions are activated, a pilot should:
choices: Comply with the published restrictions and obtain required ATS approval before flight
questions.rationale: ESCAT can impose security controls on civil air traffic; compliance with ATS/security directions is mandatory.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: ESCAT can impose security controls on civil air traffic; compliance with ATS/security directions is mandatory.

questions.question: In Southern Domestic Airspace, Class A begins generally at:
questions.rationale: Class A in Southern Domestic Airspace generally begins at FL180.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Class A in Southern Domestic Airspace generally begins at FL180.

questions.question: A two-way radio failure in controlled airspace requires the pilot of a transponder-equipped crewed aircraft to:
choices: Follow lost-communications procedures and select code 7600 as applicable
questions.rationale: 7600 is the standard transponder code for radio communication failure; pilots must also follow the applicable lost-communications procedure.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: 7600 is the standard transponder code for radio communication failure; pilots must also follow the applicable lost-communications procedure.

questions.question: Knowingly removing or interfering with an aerodrome marker, marking, light or signal used for air navigation is:
questions.rationale: Aerodrome markings, lights and signals are protected safety infrastructure under Canadian aviation rules.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: CAR Part III / TC AIM AGA
questions.learningObjective: Aerodrome markings, lights and signals are protected safety infrastructure under Canadian aviation rules.
questions.source: CAR Part III / TC AIM AGA

questions.question: In much of Northern Domestic Airspace, navigation references use:
choices: True rather than magnetic directions because magnetic references become unreliable near the magnetic pole
questions.rationale: TC AIM explains the use of true reference in NDA because of magnetic unreliability at high latitudes.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: TC AIM RAC - Northern Domestic Airspace
questions.learningObjective: TC AIM explains the use of true reference in NDA because of magnetic unreliability at high latitudes.
questions.source: TC AIM RAC - Northern Domestic Airspace

questions.question: A Class C control zone normally extends:
choices: From 3,000 ft to 12,500 ft AGL only
From the surface to a published upper limit
questions.rationale: All control zones extend from the surface; exact upper/lateral limits are published.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: All control zones extend from the surface; exact upper/lateral limits are published.

questions.question: When aeronautical radio equipment is carried and its use is required, the operator must:
choices: Maintain the required listening watch and establish/maintain communications as prescribed
questions.rationale: CAR/TC AIM radio procedures prescribe listening-watch and reporting/communication requirements in applicable airspace and MF areas.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR/TC AIM radio procedures prescribe listening-watch and reporting/communication requirements in applicable airspace and MF areas.

questions.question: Class E controlled airspace that is not a control zone:
choices: Always begins at 700 ft ASL everywhere
May begin above the surface at a published floor; its exact dimensions must be verified from charts/publications
questions.rationale: Class E dimensions vary by designation; pilots must use current charts rather than memorize one universal floor.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Class E dimensions vary by designation; pilots must use current charts rather than memorize one universal floor.

questions.question: The transponder code 7600 signifies:
questions.rationale: 7600 is the internationally recognized code for radio communications failure.
questions.learningObjective: 7600 is the internationally recognized code for radio communications failure.

questions.question: Airspace class and dimensions should be confirmed using:
choices: A remembered value from an old exam
questions.rationale: TP 15263 explicitly requires use of current aeronautical charts and publications.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 explicitly requires use of current aeronautical charts and publications.

questions.question: An aerodrome traffic frequency (ATF) is used primarily to:
choices: Facilitate traffic awareness and coordination at or near specified aerodromes where an MF is not in effect
questions.rationale: TC AIM RAC describes ATF procedures for traffic coordination at certain uncontrolled aerodromes.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TC AIM RAC describes ATF procedures for traffic coordination at certain uncontrolled aerodromes.

questions.question: At an aerodrome where an MF area is designated, pilots must:
choices: Follow the mandatory listening and reporting procedures applicable to that MF area
questions.rationale: MF procedures are mandatory and are specified in CAR 602.97-602.103 and TC AIM RAC.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: MF procedures are mandatory and are specified in CAR 602.97-602.103 and TC AIM RAC.

questions.question: A NOTAM is used to distribute:
choices: Time-critical aeronautical information concerning facilities, services, procedures or hazards
questions.rationale: NOTAMs provide timely operational information that may affect flight safety or operations.
questions.learningObjective: NOTAMs provide timely operational information that may affect flight safety or operations.

questions.question: The PIC's responsibility to avoid creating a collision hazard applies:
choices: At all times, regardless of automation or ATC service
questions.rationale: CAR Part IX and general rules impose continuing collision-avoidance responsibility on the RPAS pilot.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR Part IX and general rules impose continuing collision-avoidance responsibility on the RPAS pilot.

questions.question: Within 3 NM of the centre of a DND aerodrome, an RPAS pilot needs:
choices: Authorization from the Department of National Defence
questions.rationale: CAR 901.47(4) specifically requires DND authorization for RPAS operations within 3 NM of a DND aerodrome.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.47(4) specifically requires DND authorization for RPAS operations within 3 NM of a DND aerodrome.

questions.question: A declared RPAS model used for an Advanced operation must:
choices: Meet the technical requirements applicable to the intended operation under the declaration/Standard 922 framework
questions.rationale: The declaration identifies the technical capabilities for which the model has been shown to comply.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: The declaration identifies the technical capabilities for which the model has been shown to comply.

questions.question: If a modification changes an RPAS so it no longer conforms to its declared technical basis, the operator should:
choices: Not rely on the declaration for that capability until conformity/approval is restored
Ignore the change if flight seems normal
questions.rationale: Safety assurance depends on the configuration continuing to meet the declared technical requirements.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Safety assurance depends on the configuration continuing to meet the declared technical requirements.

questions.question: A control zone is:
choices: Controlled airspace extending upward from the surface around an aerodrome
questions.rationale: TC AIM defines control zones as controlled airspace extending upward from the surface, normally around aerodromes.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TC AIM defines control zones as controlled airspace extending upward from the surface, normally around aerodromes.

questions.question: The difference between an aerodrome and an airport is that:
choices: An airport is an aerodrome for which an airport certificate is in force; aerodrome is the broader term
questions.rationale: The Aeronautics Act/CAR framework uses aerodrome broadly and airport for a certified aerodrome.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: Aeronautics Act definitions / CAR Part III
questions.learningObjective: The Aeronautics Act/CAR framework uses aerodrome broadly and airport for a certified aerodrome.
questions.source: Aeronautics Act definitions / CAR Part III

questions.question: A pilot planning an Advanced RPAS flight near an aerodrome should check:
choices: Airspace class, published aerodrome data, traffic procedures, NOTAMs and required authorization
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires integration of charts, CFS/AIP information, airspace, aerodrome procedures and operational hazards.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires integration of charts, CFS/AIP information, airspace, aerodrome procedures and operational hazards.

questions.question: If an ATS authorization includes conditions, the RPAS pilot must:
choices: Comply with those conditions throughout the operation
questions.rationale: Controlled-airspace authorization under CAR 901.71 is operational authority subject to the terms imposed by ATS.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Controlled-airspace authorization under CAR 901.71 is operational authority subject to the terms imposed by ATS.

questions.question: Which source has the highest legal authority for a CAR requirement?
choices: The current Canadian Aviation Regulations published by Justice Laws
questions.rationale: The CARs are the legal regulation; guidance such as TC AIM explains procedures but is not itself the regulation.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: The CARs are the legal regulation; guidance such as TC AIM explains procedures but is not itself the regulation.

questions.question: Which weather phenomenon normally presents the broadest combination of severe aviation hazards?
questions.rationale: Thunderstorms can combine turbulence, lightning, hail, heavy precipitation, icing, wind shear and microbursts.
questions.learningObjective: Thunderstorms can combine turbulence, lightning, hail, heavy precipitation, icing, wind shear and microbursts.

questions.question: A gust front is:
choices: The centre of a high-pressure system
The leading edge of cool outflow spreading outward from a thunderstorm
questions.rationale: Thunderstorm downdraft outflow can produce a sharp wind shift and strong gusts ahead of the storm.
questions.learningObjective: Thunderstorm downdraft outflow can produce a sharp wind shift and strong gusts ahead of the storm.

questions.question: Approximately 78% of dry air is:
questions.rationale: Nitrogen is the dominant constituent of dry air.
questions.learningObjective: Nitrogen is the dominant constituent of dry air.

questions.question: In Canadian METARs, prevailing visibility is normally reported in:
questions.rationale: Canadian METAR visibility is commonly expressed in statute miles, with metric conventions used for certain runway visual range products.
questions.learningObjective: Canadian METAR visibility is commonly expressed in statute miles, with metric conventions used for certain runway visual range products.

questions.question: A surface high-pressure system is generally associated with:
choices: Strong persistent ascent at its centre
A warm front at its centre
questions.rationale: High-pressure systems feature sinking motion and outward surface flow, generally favouring stability.
questions.learningObjective: High-pressure systems feature sinking motion and outward surface flow, generally favouring stability.

questions.question: A microburst is especially hazardous because it can produce:
choices: Severe localized wind shear and rapidly changing wind
questions.rationale: Microbursts create intense downdrafts and divergent surface winds over a small area.
questions.learningObjective: Microbursts create intense downdrafts and divergent surface winds over a small area.

questions.question: A SIGMET is intended to advise of:
choices: Significant en-route weather phenomena potentially hazardous to aircraft
questions.rationale: SIGMETs provide warnings of significant meteorological phenomena hazardous to aviation.
questions.learningObjective: SIGMETs provide warnings of significant meteorological phenomena hazardous to aviation.

questions.question: A METAR is primarily:
choices: A routine aviation weather observation for an aerodrome/station
questions.rationale: METAR is the standard routine aerodrome weather report.
questions.learningObjective: METAR is the standard routine aerodrome weather report.

questions.question: A SPECI is:
choices: A special weather report issued when specified significant changes occur
questions.rationale: SPECI is a special aerodrome meteorological report triggered by specified criteria.
questions.learningObjective: SPECI is a special aerodrome meteorological report triggered by specified criteria.

questions.question: The code 'BKN' in a METAR means:
questions.rationale: BKN denotes broken cloud coverage, an aviation ceiling layer when applicable.
questions.knowledgeTopic: TC AIM MET - METAR Cloud Amount
questions.learningObjective: BKN denotes broken cloud coverage, an aviation ceiling layer when applicable.
questions.source: TC AIM MET - METAR Cloud Amount

questions.question: The code 'OVC' means:
questions.rationale: OVC indicates 8/8 cloud coverage.
questions.knowledgeTopic: TC AIM MET - METAR Cloud Amount
questions.learningObjective: OVC indicates 8/8 cloud coverage.
questions.source: TC AIM MET - METAR Cloud Amount

questions.question: A ceiling is based on:
choices: The lowest BKN or OVC layer, or vertical visibility into an obscuration, as applicable
questions.rationale: Aviation ceiling is the height of the lowest broken/overcast layer or vertical visibility into an obscuration.
questions.learningObjective: Aviation ceiling is the height of the lowest broken/overcast layer or vertical visibility into an obscuration.

questions.question: The dewpoint spread becomes smaller as:
questions.rationale: Temperature approaching dewpoint indicates rising relative humidity and increased likelihood of cloud/fog.
questions.learningObjective: Temperature approaching dewpoint indicates rising relative humidity and increased likelihood of cloud/fog.

questions.question: Radiation fog is most favoured by:
choices: Clear skies, light wind, moist low-level air and nighttime surface cooling
questions.rationale: Radiational cooling under light winds can cool near-surface air to saturation.
questions.learningObjective: Radiational cooling under light winds can cool near-surface air to saturation.

questions.question: Advection fog forms when:
choices: A thunderstorm downdraft reaches the ground
Moist air moves over a colder surface and is cooled to saturation
questions.rationale: Advection transports moist air over a cold surface, cooling it toward dewpoint.
questions.learningObjective: Advection transports moist air over a cold surface, cooling it toward dewpoint.

questions.question: Upslope fog/cloud can develop when:
choices: Moist air is forced to rise along terrain and cools adiabatically
questions.rationale: Orographic ascent cools air and can produce saturation/cloud.
questions.learningObjective: Orographic ascent cools air and can produce saturation/cloud.

questions.question: A cold front normally has:
choices: Warm air replacing cold air with no lifting
Advancing colder air undercutting warmer air
questions.rationale: Cold fronts are boundaries where colder air advances, forcing warmer air upward.
questions.learningObjective: Cold fronts are boundaries where colder air advances, forcing warmer air upward.

questions.question: Compared with a warm front, a cold front commonly produces:
choices: A narrower band of more abrupt weather and stronger wind shifts
questions.rationale: Cold fronts often have steeper slopes and more abrupt weather changes.
questions.learningObjective: Cold fronts often have steeper slopes and more abrupt weather changes.

questions.question: A warm front is characterized by:
choices: Warm air advancing and overrunning retreating colder air
questions.rationale: Warm frontal lifting is gradual and often produces layered cloud/precipitation.
questions.learningObjective: Warm frontal lifting is gradual and often produces layered cloud/precipitation.

questions.question: An occluded front develops when:
choices: A cold front overtakes a warm front
questions.rationale: Occlusion occurs as the faster-moving cold front catches the warm front.
questions.learningObjective: Occlusion occurs as the faster-moving cold front catches the warm front.

questions.question: A TROWAL is:
choices: A trough of warm air aloft associated with an occluded system
questions.rationale: TROWAL means trough of warm air aloft, an important feature of occluded cyclones.
questions.learningObjective: TROWAL means trough of warm air aloft, an important feature of occluded cyclones.

questions.question: The GFA system divides Canada into:
questions.rationale: The Canadian Graphic Area Forecast program uses seven GFA regions.
questions.learningObjective: The Canadian Graphic Area Forecast program uses seven GFA regions.

questions.question: Convection is vertical motion caused primarily by:
choices: Unequal heating and buoyancy, with warm air rising
questions.rationale: Surface heating can create buoyant thermals and convective cloud.
questions.learningObjective: Surface heating can create buoyant thermals and convective cloud.

questions.question: Orographic lift occurs when:
choices: Air is forced upward by rising terrain
questions.rationale: Terrain mechanically forces air to rise and cool.
questions.learningObjective: Terrain mechanically forces air to rise and cool.

questions.question: TAFs are normally issued on a scheduled cycle:
choices: At specified routine times, commonly every six hours for many Canadian TAF locations
questions.rationale: TAFs are scheduled aerodrome forecasts; issue frequency/validity is specified in Canadian meteorological services.
questions.learningObjective: TAFs are scheduled aerodrome forecasts; issue frequency/validity is specified in Canadian meteorological services.

questions.question: A TAF describes expected weather:
choices: At and in the vicinity of a specified aerodrome for a defined validity period
questions.rationale: TAFs are terminal aerodrome forecasts with a defined validity period.
questions.learningObjective: TAFs are terminal aerodrome forecasts with a defined validity period.

questions.question: The group 'TEMPO' in a TAF indicates:
choices: Temporary fluctuations expected during the stated period
questions.rationale: TEMPO identifies temporary forecast conditions expected to occur for limited portions of the period.
questions.knowledgeTopic: TC AIM MET - TAF Change Groups
questions.learningObjective: TEMPO identifies temporary forecast conditions expected to occur for limited portions of the period.
questions.source: TC AIM MET - TAF Change Groups

questions.question: The group 'BECMG' in a TAF indicates:
choices: Conditions expected to become the stated values during the indicated period
questions.rationale: BECMG denotes a gradual or indeterminate-time transition within the stated period.
questions.knowledgeTopic: TC AIM MET - TAF Change Groups
questions.learningObjective: BECMG denotes a gradual or indeterminate-time transition within the stated period.
questions.source: TC AIM MET - TAF Change Groups

questions.question: The group 'FM' in a TAF indicates:
choices: A relatively rapid change beginning at the specified time
questions.rationale: FM marks a new forecast condition beginning from a specified time.
questions.knowledgeTopic: TC AIM MET - TAF Change Groups
questions.learningObjective: FM marks a new forecast condition beginning from a specified time.
questions.source: TC AIM MET - TAF Change Groups

questions.question: A GFA Clouds and Weather chart includes:
choices: Major cloud, precipitation, visibility and weather features for the forecast region
